target.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadCronQuarantineFile` in `src/cron/store.ts` reads the cron quarantine sidecar with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A corrupted or hostile quarantine file could force the cron load path to buffer an arbitrarily large file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Quarantine sidecars are small JSON files. An 8 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate quarantine state while preventing the cron load path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Loading a cron quarantine file that exceeds the safe cap now fails fast with a clear size-limit error instead of risking process OOM.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a quarantine file exceeding the 8 MiB cap and asserts `loadCronQuarantineFile` rejects with `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/store.test.ts --run` passes (46/46 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I created a cron quarantine sidecar file larger than the new 8 MiB cap and ran `loadCronQuarantineFile`. The helper rejects the file before JSON parsing:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/store.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |cron| src/cron/store.test.ts (46 tests) 468ms
     ✓ rejects oversized quarantine files to prevent OOM
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  46 passed (46)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.88s
```

The oversized sidecar is rejected with `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`, preventing the cron load path from buffering a corrupted or hostile quarantine file.
